result.summary: Full-time employees receive their usual compensation during jury service; employers with 5 or fewer full-time employees may ask the court to postpone service when a second employee would be out at the same time

rules.title: California Voting Leave

citations.source: Cal. Elec. Code §§14000-14003 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Colorado Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Regular wages up to $50 a day for the first 3 days of juror service, for full-time, part-time, temporary and casual employees

rules.title: Connecticut Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Full-time employees receive regular wages for the first 5 days of jury service

rules.title: District of Columbia Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Employers with more than 10 employees pay full-time employees regular wages, less the jury fee, for the first 5 days of service

rules.title: District of Columbia Voting Leave

result.summary: At least 2 hours of paid leave to vote in person, requested with reasonable notice (7 days where no policy says otherwise); the employer may require early voting or set the time

citations.source: D.C. Code §1-1001.07a (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Georgia Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 2 hours of unpaid leave to vote (or vote early) with reasonable notice; the employer may set the hours

rules.title: Iowa Voting Leave

citations.source: Iowa Code §49.109 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Illinois Voting Leave

result.summary: 2 hours of paid leave to vote, requested before election day, when the shift begins less than 2 hours after polls open and ends less than 2 hours before they close

rules.title: Kansas Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 2 consecutive hours of paid leave to vote unless the employee has 2 consecutive non-working hours while polls are open; the employer may set the time but not during the lunch period

citations.source: Kan. Stat. Ann. §25-418 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Kentucky Voting Leave

result.summary: At least 4 hours of unpaid leave to vote or to apply for or cast an absentee ballot, requested before election day; the employer may set the hours

citations.source: Ky. Rev. Stat. §118.035 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Louisiana Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Regular wages for one day of jury service; the employer may not require the employee to use annual, sick or vacation leave

rules.title: Massachusetts Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Regular wages for the first 3 days of juror service, for full-time, part-time, temporary and casual employees

rules.title: Massachusetts Voting Leave

result.summary: Employees of manufacturing, mechanical or mercantile establishments may take unpaid leave during the first 2 hours polls are open, on request

citations.source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 149, §178 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Maryland Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 2 hours of paid leave to vote (proof of voting required) unless the employee has 2 continuous non-working hours while polls are open

citations.source: Md. Code, Elec. Law §10-315 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Minnesota Voting Leave

result.summary: Paid time off for as long as needed to vote and return to work, without penalty or deduction

citations.source: Minn. Stat. §204C.04 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Missouri Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 3 hours of paid leave to vote, requested before election day, unless the employee has 3 continuous non-working hours while polls are open; the employer may set the hours

citations.source: Mo. Rev. Stat. §115.639 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Nebraska Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Normal wages during jury service, less the juror fee received; the employee gives reasonable notice

rules.title: Nebraska Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 2 consecutive hours of paid leave to vote, requested before or on election day, unless the employee has 2 consecutive non-working hours while polls are open

citations.source: Neb. Rev. Stat. §32-922 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: New Mexico Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 2 hours of paid leave to vote unless the shift starts more than 2 hours after polls open or ends more than 3 hours before they close

citations.source: N.M. Stat. Ann. §1-12-42 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Nevada Jury Duty Shift Limits

result.summary: The employer may not require work within 8 hours of the time the employee must report for jury service, nor between 5 p.m. and 3 a.m. on a day the employee served 4 or more hours including travel

rules.title: Nevada Voting Leave

result.summary: Paid leave to vote of 1 hour (polling place within 2 miles), 2 hours (2 to 10 miles) or 3 hours (over 10 miles), requested before election day, when voting outside working hours is impracticable

citations.source: Nev. Rev. Stat. §293.463 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: New York Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Employers with 10 or more employees pay the first $40 of the daily wage for the first 3 days of jury service

citations.source: N.Y. Elec. Law §3-110 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Ohio Voting Leave

citations.source: Ohio Rev. Code §3599.06 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Oklahoma Voting Leave

citations.source: 26 Okla. Stat. §7-101 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: South Dakota Voting Leave

citations.source: S.D. Codified Laws §12-3-5 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Tennessee Jury Duty Pay

result.summary: Employers with 5 or more employees pay usual wages, less the jury fee, to employees with at least 6 months of service

citations.source: Tex. Elec. Code §276.004 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Utah Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 2 hours of paid leave to vote, requested before election day, unless the employee has 3 or more non-working hours while polls are open; the employer may set the hours

citations.source: Utah Code §20A-3a-105 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Wisconsin Voting Leave

result.summary: Up to 3 consecutive hours of unpaid leave to vote, requested before election day; the employer may set the time

citations.source: Wis. Stat. §6.76 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: West Virginia Voting Leave

citations.source: W. Va. Code §3-1-42 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Wyoming Voting Leave

rules.title: Arizona — Crime Victim Leave (court proceedings, 50+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: attend court proceedings and obtain or enforce protective orders as a crime victim

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees must allow a crime victim (or immediate family of a victim) unpaid leave to attend court proceedings and obtain protective orders; accrued paid leave may be used. Safe leave for domestic violence is also a use of Arizona earned paid sick time (ARS 23-373).

rules.title: California — Victim Leave for Court and Safety (all employers)

params.covered_reasons: judicial proceedings related to the crime; relief such as restraining orders for the safety of the employee or a child

result.summary: All employers: no discharge or retaliation for time off to appear in court as a crime victim or to seek a restraining order or other relief for safety (Lab. Code 230(c), (e)); reasonable safety accommodations required on request (230(f)). Employee may use accrued paid leave. Expanded 2025 (AB 2499) to victims of 'qualifying acts of violence' and moved to Gov. Code 12945.8 for CRD enforcement.

rules.title: California — Victim Leave for Medical, Counseling and Relocation (25+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical attention, victim services, counseling, safety planning, relocation

result.summary: Employers with 25 or more employees must also allow unpaid time off for medical attention, victim services, psychological counseling, safety planning and relocation (Lab. Code 230.1); from 2025 the right is in Gov. Code 12945.8 and family members of victims are covered for certain purposes.

rules.title: Colorado — Domestic Violence Leave (3 days, 50+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: protective orders, medical care, counseling, relocation, legal assistance

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees must give an employee with 12 months of service up to 3 working days of leave in any 12-month period for domestic abuse, stalking, sexual assault or another DV-related crime; unpaid unless the employee elects accrued paid leave. Safe time is also a use of Colorado paid sick leave (CRS 8-13.3-404).

rules.title: Connecticut — Family Violence and Sexual Assault Leave (12 days, 3+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical care or counseling, victim services, relocation, civil or criminal proceedings

result.summary: Employers with 3 or more employees must allow paid or unpaid leave reasonably necessary for a victim of family violence or sexual assault; unpaid leave may be limited to 12 days a calendar year. Up to 7 days' notice may be required when foreseeable.

rules.title: Florida — Domestic Violence Leave (3 days, 50+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: injunctions, medical care or counseling, victim services, new housing, legal help

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees must give an employee with 3 months of service up to 3 working days of leave in any 12-month period when the employee or a household member is a victim of domestic or sexual violence; paid or unpaid at the employer's option; other accrued leave must be used first unless waived.

rules.title: Hawaii — Domestic or Sexual Violence Leave (30 days, 50+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical care, victim services, counseling, relocation, legal action

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees must allow up to 30 days of unpaid leave per calendar year when the employee or the employee's minor child is a victim of domestic or sexual violence.

rules.title: Hawaii — Domestic or Sexual Violence Leave (5 days, under 50 employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical care, victim services, counseling, relocation, legal action

result.summary: Employers with 49 or fewer employees must allow up to 5 days of unpaid leave per calendar year when the employee or the employee's minor child is a victim of domestic or sexual violence.

rules.title: Illinois VESSA — 12 weeks (50+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical care or recovery, victim services, safety planning or relocation, legal assistance and court proceedings

result.summary: Victims' Economic Security and Safety Act: employers with 50 or more employees must give up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave per 12 months to an employee who is, or whose family or household member is, a victim of domestic, sexual or gender violence or another crime of violence (2024 amendment adds funeral and bereavement time for a family member killed in a crime).

rules.title: Illinois VESSA — 8 weeks (15-49 employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical care or recovery, victim services, safety planning or relocation, legal assistance and court proceedings

result.summary: Employers with 15 to 49 employees must give up to 8 weeks of unpaid VESSA leave per 12 months.

rules.title: Illinois VESSA — 4 weeks (1-14 employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical care or recovery, victim services, safety planning or relocation, legal assistance and court proceedings

result.summary: From 2017-01-01 employers with 1 to 14 employees must give up to 4 weeks of unpaid VESSA leave per 12 months.

rules.title: Iowa — Victim and Witness Court Leave

params.covered_reasons: attend criminal proceedings as a victim or witness, including domestic abuse proceedings

result.summary: An employer may not discharge or penalize an employee for taking time off to attend criminal proceedings as a victim or to honor a subpoena as a witness; unpaid.

rules.title: Kansas — Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Leave (8 days)

params.covered_reasons: restraining orders, medical care, shelter or crisis services, court appearances

result.summary: Employees who are victims of domestic violence or sexual assault may take up to 8 days of leave per calendar year for protective orders, medical care, shelter or rape-crisis services and court appearances; accrued paid leave first, then unpaid. Documentation within 48 hours.

rules.title: Maine — Leave for Victims of Violence (reasonable and necessary)

params.covered_reasons: court proceedings, medical care, victim services for the employee or a family member

result.summary: Employers must grant reasonable and necessary leave, with or without pay, for an employee who is (or whose parent, spouse or child is) a victim of violence, assault, sexual assault, stalking or domestic violence to prepare for and attend court, receive medical treatment or obtain services; the employee must not be the perpetrator.

rules.title: Massachusetts — Domestic Violence Leave (15 days, 50+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical attention, counseling, victim services, legal assistance, housing, protective orders, court, child custody matters

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees must give up to 15 days of leave in any 12-month period when the employee or a family member is a victim of abusive behavior; paid or unpaid at the employer's option; employer may require other leave be exhausted first; employees must be notified of the right.

rules.title: Minnesota — Leave to Seek an Order for Protection

params.covered_reasons: attend court to obtain or enforce an order for protection or harassment restraining order for the employee or a minor child

result.summary: No employer may discharge or discipline an employee for taking reasonable time off to obtain or attempt to obtain relief under an order for protection (Minn. Stat. 518B.01) for the employee or a minor child; unpaid. Safe time is also a use of Earned Sick and Safe Time (181.9447).

rules.title: Missouri — Victims Economic Safety and Security Act (2 weeks, 50+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical care, victim services, counseling, safety planning or relocation, legal assistance

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees must give up to 2 workweeks of unpaid leave per 12 months to an employee who is, or whose family or household member is, a victim of domestic or sexual violence.

rules.title: Missouri — Victims Economic Safety and Security Act (1 week, 20-49 employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical care, victim services, counseling, safety planning or relocation, legal assistance

result.summary: Employers with 20 to 49 employees must give up to 1 workweek of unpaid leave per 12 months for domestic or sexual violence.

rules.title: Nevada — Domestic Violence Leave (160 hours)

params.covered_reasons: diagnosis and treatment, counseling, court proceedings, safety planning

result.summary: Employees with 90 days of service who are (or whose family or household member is) a victim of domestic violence or sexual assault get up to 160 hours of leave in the 12 months after the act, paid or unpaid at the employer's option, consecutive or intermittent; reasonable accommodations also required (NRS 613.222).

rules.title: New Hampshire — Crime Victim Employment Leave (25+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: attend court or other legal or investigative proceedings associated with the prosecution of the crime

result.summary: Employers with 25 or more employees must allow a crime victim (or immediate family of a homicide or incapacitated victim) unpaid leave to attend court and other proceedings associated with the prosecution of the crime; accrued paid leave may be required to be used.

rules.title: New Jersey SAFE Act — 20 days (25+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: medical attention, victim services, counseling, safety planning or relocation, legal assistance, court proceedings

result.summary: Security and Financial Empowerment Act: employers with 25 or more employees must give an employee with 12 months and 1,000 hours of service up to 20 days of unpaid leave in the 12 months after an incident of domestic violence or a sexually violent offense against the employee or a family member; may be intermittent in full-day units; poster required.

rules.title: New Mexico — Promoting Financial Independence for Victims of Domestic Abuse Act (14 days)

params.covered_reasons: protective orders, court proceedings, law enforcement, medical care or counseling for the employee or a family member

result.summary: All employers must allow intermittent paid or unpaid leave of up to 14 days per calendar year, in increments of up to 8 hours a day, for an employee who is (or whose family member is) a victim of domestic abuse to obtain orders of protection, meet with law enforcement or attend court, medical or counseling appointments.

rules.title: New York — Reasonable Accommodation for Domestic Violence Victims

params.covered_reasons: medical attention, victim services, counseling, safety planning or relocation, legal assistance and court proceedings

result.summary: Employers must provide reasonable accommodation, including a reasonable amount of time off, to an employee who is a victim of domestic violence for medical care, victim services, counseling, relocation or legal proceedings unless undue hardship; accrued paid leave may be charged first (Exec. Law 296(22)). Safe leave is also a use of NY paid sick leave (Labor Law 196-b).

rules.title: North Carolina — Leave to Seek a Domestic Violence Protective Order

params.covered_reasons: obtain or attempt to obtain relief under Chapter 50B (domestic violence protective orders) for the employee or a minor child

result.summary: No employer may discharge, demote or discipline an employee for taking reasonable time off to obtain or attempt to obtain a domestic violence protective order; unpaid, employee must follow the employer's usual time-off procedures where practicable.

rules.title: Oregon — Leave for Victims of Domestic Violence, Harassment, Sexual Assault, Bias or Stalking (6+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: legal or law enforcement assistance, medical treatment, counseling, victim services, relocation or safety measures

result.summary: Employers with 6 or more employees must allow reasonable unpaid leave (accrued paid leave may be used) for an employee who is (or whose minor child or dependent is) a victim of domestic violence, harassment, sexual assault, bias crime or stalking, and must provide reasonable safety accommodations (ORS 659A.290). Paid safe leave also available under Oregon sick time (ORS 653.616).

rules.title: Rhode Island — Crime Victim Court Leave (50+ employees)

params.covered_reasons: attend court proceedings related to the crime

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees may not discharge or penalize a crime victim (or qualifying family member) for attending court proceedings related to the crime; unpaid, employer may require 30 days' notice where practicable. Safe leave is also a use of RI paid sick and safe leave (RIGL 28-57).

rules.title: Vermont — Crime Victim Leave (court proceedings)

params.covered_reasons: attend depositions and court proceedings related to a listed crime, including relief from abuse hearings

result.summary: An employee who has worked an average of 20 hours a week for 6 months and is a victim of a listed crime (or the family member of a homicide victim) may take unpaid leave to attend depositions and court proceedings; accrued paid leave may be used; employer continues benefits at the employee's expense.

rules.title: Virginia — Crime Victim Court Leave

params.covered_reasons: attend criminal proceedings as a victim, after notice to the employer

result.summary: Employers may not discharge or discipline a crime victim for leaving work to attend criminal proceedings relating to the crime, after a copy of the notice of proceedings is given; unpaid, and the employer may limit leave when it creates an undue hardship.

rules.title: Washington — Domestic Violence Leave (reasonable leave, all employers)

params.covered_reasons: legal or law enforcement assistance, medical treatment, counseling, victim services, relocation or safety planning

result.summary: All employers must allow reasonable leave (paid from accrued leave, otherwise unpaid), intermittent or on a reduced schedule, for an employee who is (or whose family member is) a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, and must provide reasonable safety accommodations. Safe leave is also a use of WA paid sick leave (RCW 49.46.210).

rules.title: USERRA — Uniformed Services Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: uniformed services (active duty, reserve and National Guard federal duty, training)

result.summary: All employers must grant unpaid leave for service in the uniformed services and reemploy the employee in the escalator position after up to 5 cumulative years of service, with no discrimination or retaliation; health coverage continues up to 24 months at the employee's expense. State-ordered National Guard duty is covered only by state law.

rules.title: California — Military Spouse Leave (10 days, 25+ employees)

params.trigger: service member on leave from deployment during a period of military conflict

result.summary: Employers with 25 or more employees must give an employee who works 20 or more hours a week up to 10 days of unpaid leave while their spouse or domestic partner is on leave from deployment during a military conflict; 2 business days' notice.

rules.title: Illinois Family Military Leave Act — 30 days (51+ employees)

params.trigger: family member called to military service lasting longer than 30 days

result.summary: Employers with more than 50 employees must give an employee with 12 months and 1,250 hours of service up to 30 days of unpaid leave during a family member's call to military service of more than 30 days; other paid leave (except sick and disability) must be exhausted first; 14 days' notice for leave of 5 or more days. Expanded 2022 to include children and grandparents.

rules.title: Illinois Family Military Leave Act — 15 days (15-50 employees)

params.trigger: family member called to military service lasting longer than 30 days

result.summary: Employers with 15 to 50 employees must give up to 15 days of unpaid family military leave under the same conditions.

rules.title: Indiana — Military Family Leave (10 days, 50+ employees)

params.trigger: family member ordered to active duty: 30 days before orders take effect, during the member's leave, or 30 days after active duty ends

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees must give an employee with 12 months and 1,500 hours of service up to 10 days of unpaid leave per year around a family member's active duty; employee may elect accrued paid leave; 30 days' notice unless orders give less.

rules.title: Maine — Family Military Leave (15 days, 15+ employees)

params.trigger: family member deployed for 180 days or more: the 15 days before and after deployment and during the member's leave

result.summary: Employers with 15 or more employees must give an employee with 12 months and 1,250 hours of service up to 15 days of unpaid leave per deployment when a spouse, domestic partner or child is deployed for 180 days or more.

rules.title: Minnesota — Leave for Injury or Death of a Service Member Family Member (10 days)

params.trigger: family member injured or killed while on active duty

result.summary: All employers must give up to 10 working days of unpaid leave to an employee whose immediate family member is injured or killed on active duty (181.947), and up to one day for a send-off or homecoming ceremony (181.948); employer may require other paid leave (not sick leave) be used first.

rules.title: Nebraska Family Military Leave Act — 30 days (51+ employees)

params.trigger: family member called to military service for more than 179 days

result.summary: Employers with more than 50 employees must give an employee with 12 months and 1,250 hours of service up to 30 days of unpaid leave during a spouse's or child's call to service of more than 179 days; 14 days' notice for leave over 5 days.

rules.title: Nebraska Family Military Leave Act — 15 days (15-50 employees)

params.trigger: family member called to military service for more than 179 days

result.summary: Employers with 15 to 50 employees must give up to 15 days of unpaid family military leave under the same conditions.

rules.title: New York — Military Spouse Leave (10 days, 20+ employees)

params.trigger: spouse on leave from deployment to a combat theater or zone of operations

result.summary: Employers with 20 or more employees at one site must give an employee who works 20 or more hours a week up to 10 days of unpaid leave while a spouse on active duty in a combat theater or zone is on leave.

rules.title: Ohio — Military Family Leave (10 days or 80 hours, 50+ employees)

params.covered_relationships: spouse, parent (of a child), or the employee is the parent of the service member
params.trigger: family member called to active duty for longer than 30 days, or injured or hospitalized while on duty

result.summary: Employers with 50 or more employees must give an employee with 12 consecutive months and 1,250 hours of service up to 10 days or 80 hours (whichever is less) of unpaid leave per calendar year when a spouse or child is called to active duty of more than 30 days or is injured; leave only in the 2 weeks before and after deployment or during the member's leave; 14 days' notice.

rules.title: Oregon Military Family Leave Act (14 days, 25+ employees)

params.trigger: spouse called to active duty or on leave from deployment

result.summary: Employers with 25 or more employees must give an employee who works 20 or more hours a week up to 14 days of unpaid leave per deployment when a spouse or domestic partner is notified of an impending call to active duty or is on leave from deployment; OFLA job protections apply.

rules.title: Rhode Island Military Family Relief Act (15 or 30 days, 15+ employees)

params.trigger: family member called to military service lasting longer than 30 days

result.summary: Employers with 15 to 50 employees must give up to 15 days, and employers with more than 50 employees up to 30 days, of unpaid leave to an employee with 12 months and 1,250 hours of service during a spouse's or child's call to military service of more than 30 days; 14 days' notice for leave of 5 or more days.

rules.title: Washington — Military Family Leave (15 days)

params.trigger: spouse notified of an impending call to active duty or on leave from deployment during a period of military conflict

result.summary: All employers must give an employee who works an average of 20 or more hours a week up to 15 days of unpaid leave per deployment when a spouse or domestic partner is called to active duty or is on leave from deployment during a military conflict; employee may elect accrued paid leave; 5 business days' notice.
